title: AI’s Electricity Demand Is Not the Real Problem. Its Inflexibility Is
excerpt: Flexible grid connections, workload shifting, batteries and smarter siting could make data centers valuable grid assets rather than merely another source of...
content_html:
Leon Stille

Sat, August 1, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT 7 min read

The electricity demand created by artificial intelligence is usually presented as a simple supply problem. AI requires increasingly large data centers, those facilities consume enormous amounts of electricity, and utilities must somehow build enough power plants to serve them.

The numbers appear to support the alarm. Data centers consumed around 485 terawatt-hours of electricity globally in 2025. The International Energy Agency expects this to rise to approximately 950 TWh by 2030, while consumption from AI-focused facilities could triple. Some proposed AI campuses will require several gigawatts of capacity—more than many cities.

Yet the global numbers hide the real problem. Data centers are expected to account for only around 3% of worldwide electricity demand by 2030. Their impact is serious, but it is not remotely large enough to overwhelm the global electricity system.

The difficulty is that AI demand is arriving in very large blocks, in very specific locations, and on timelines that are much shorter than those required to build grids and power plants.

AI does not primarily have an electricity problem. It has an inflexibility problem.

The Local Grid Matters More Than the Global Total

The IEA expects data-center electricity consumption to roughly double between 2025 and 2030. That is substantial, but data centers will still account for only a fraction of total global demand growth. Industrial motors, air conditioning, electric vehicles and wider electrification will collectively add considerably more.

However, those loads are widely distributed. A million electric vehicles charge at thousands of locations. Air-conditioning demand is spread across millions of buildings. A new AI campus can add hundreds of megawatts behind a single grid connection.

Almost half of existing U.S. data-center capacity is concentrated in five regional clusters. Meanwhile, the IEA estimates that around half of the data centers currently under development in the United States are again being built in established clusters.

Related: Finland's Sand Battery Cuts Emissions 70% Without a Single Rare Earth

This creates an increasingly strange market. Technology companies are prepared to invest billions in computing infrastructure that can be constructed within two or three years, but the transmission lines required to supply it may take four to eight years. Waiting times for transformers, cables and gas turbines have also increased.

The IEA estimates that approximately 20% of planned data-center projects could face delays if these electricity-sector bottlenecks are not addressed.

content_html_zh:
莱昂·斯蒂尔

2026 年 8 月 1 日星期六，美国东部时间下午 5:00 阅读 7 分钟

人工智能产生的电力需求通常表现为一个简单的供应问题。 人工智能需要越来越大的数据中心，这些设施消耗大量的电力，公用事业公司必须以某种方式建造足够的发电厂来为其服务。

这些数字似乎支持了警报。 2025 年，全球数据中心消耗约 485 太瓦时电力。 国际能源署预计，到 2030 年，这一数字将增至约 950 太瓦时，而以人工智能为重点的设施的消耗量可能会增加两倍。 一些拟议的人工智能园区将需要数千兆瓦的容量——比许多城市还要多。

然而全球数字掩盖了真正的问题。 预计到 2030 年，数据中心将仅占全球电力需求的 3% 左右。 它们的影响是严重的，但还远没有大到足以压倒全球电力系统。

困难在于，人工智能的需求是在非常大的区块、非常特定的地点到达的，而且其时间表比建设电网和发电厂所需的时间表要短得多。

人工智能主要不存在电力问题。 它有一个不灵活的问题。

本地电网比全球电网更重要

IEA 预计 2025 年至 2030 年间数据中心的电力消耗将大约翻一番。 这是一个很大的数字，但数据中心仍仅占全球总需求增长的一小部分。 工业电机、空调、电动汽车和更广泛的电气化将共同带来更多的增长。

然而，这些负载分布广泛。 一百万辆电动汽车在数千个地点充电。 空调需求遍布数百万座建筑物。 一个新的人工智能园区可以在单个电网连接后增加数百兆瓦的电力。

美国现有数据中心容量的近一半集中在五个区域集群。 与此同时，国际能源署估计，美国目前正在开发的数据中心约有一半再次建在已建立的集群中。

相关：芬兰的沙电池在不使用任何稀土的情况下减少了 70% 的排放

这创造了一个越来越奇怪的市场。 科技公司准备投资数十亿美元建设可在两到三年内建成的计算基础设施，但为其供电所需的传输线路可能需要四到八年的时间。 变压器、电缆和燃气轮机的等待时间也增加了。

IEA 估计，如果不解决这些电力部门的瓶颈，大约 20% 的计划数据中心项目可能会面临延误。
